F1.label: Certainty versus qualified exploration
F1.description: Certainty contrasts with hedging, qualification, curiosity and open-minded language in this saved orientation.
F1.higher: More certain wording and less qualification or exploration.
F1.lower: More qualified, tentative or exploratory wording.

F2.label: Disappointment versus positive tone
F2.description: Expressed disappointment contrasts with joy, positive valence, hope and pride in this saved orientation.
F2.higher: More expressed disappointment and less positive or hopeful language.
F2.lower: More positive and hopeful language, with less expressed disappointment.

F3.label: Direct and organized argument or address
F3.description: Directness, persistence, persuasion, organization, evidence language and viewer address tend to occur together.
F3.higher: More direct, sustained and organized argument or audience address.
F3.lower: Less of this direct, sustained argument or address pattern.

F4.label: Humor and imaginative language
F4.description: Humor, expressed amusement, irony and imaginative language share this pattern.
F4.higher: More humor, amusement, irony or imaginative wording.
F4.lower: Less of these expressed humorous or imaginative cues.

F5.label: Lower expressed care and affiliation
F5.description: Compassion, respect, care and trust have negative loadings in the saved orientation. This describes language, not whether someone is caring or trustworthy.
F5.higher: Less expressed care, respect, trust or affiliative language.
F5.lower: More expressed care, respect, trust or affiliative language.

F6.label: Calm versus energetic language
F6.description: Calm language contrasts with emotional activation, verbal energy and intensifiers.
F6.higher: Calmer, less activated and less intensified language.
F6.lower: More energetic, activated or intensified language.

F7.label: Self-critical and worried language
F7.description: Self-criticism, embarrassment, fear, worry and sadness cluster together. These are textual cues, not a diagnosis or a verified private emotional state.
F7.higher: More self-critical, worried or vulnerable language.
F7.lower: Less of these expressed self-critical or worried cues.

F8.label: Lower rebuttal and conflict language
F8.description: Conflict, rebuttal, represented other voices and deflection have negative loadings in the saved orientation. Represented voices may be quotations, not additional live speakers.
F8.higher: Less conflict, rebuttal, other-voice representation or deflection.
F8.lower: More conflict, rebuttal, other-voice representation or deflection.

F9.label: Persuasion versus narrative and scene setting
F9.description: Persuasion contrasts with narrative and scene setting in this saved orientation, with narrative and scene-setting questions having the larger absolute loadings.
F9.higher: Less narrative or scene setting, with relatively more persuasion.
F9.lower: More narrative or scene-setting language relative to persuasion.
